doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Musical family and the decision to be a musician
summary: Vaché's father and brother were musicians and he never considered anything else; born 1953, he grew up on records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Oh gosh. Well I come from a musical family. My brother is a professional musician, my father was at one point a professional musician but felt he couldn’t support a family on it so ended up just working weekends and stuff and playing. He played at Nick’s and Condon’s back in the ‘30s and so forth. And at this particular point I would say I can’t think of anything else that I could have done. I had never had any interest in anything else. I mean I listened to this kind of music since before I knew what I was listening to, when I was a baby in the crib. So it never occurred to me to do anything else.
It’s interesting, those early impressions, that they take root with some people and with some people they don’t. You must have had an inherent music talent that latched on to that kind of jazz music.

Yeah I would guess so. It’s all abstract, so it’s kind of hard to really pin down. But on the same token I would think that both my brother and I inherited some form of musical talent that gravitated us toward this kind of music, for improvisational music especially. It’s really kind of hard to explain. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
Yeah. Well you were born when?
Okay, so the music that was being played most prevalently on the radio by the time you were really aware of it, would have been like early rock & roll I suppose.
But also things like Peggy Lee and Ray Conniff and all that. But what did you hear in your house?
